chunks: He said: The obligations have swept them away, O Commander of the Faithful!

key_terms.أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (title for Imam Ali)

ai.seo_question: What does 'dhadha'at al-huquq' mean in the context of lost wealth in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Sharif al-Radi records this concise dialogue where the phrase 'ذَعْذَعَتْها الحُقُوقُ' (the rights shook/dispersed it) metaphorically describes how the heavy burden of financial obligations, such as debt or khums, caused the camels to scatter or be lost. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the tangible, often disruptive, priority of fulfilling divine and social rights (Huquq) over the mere retention of wealth, reflecting the practical realities of the early Islamic community's economic life.
